criterion: The long-horizon effort ladder's frozen configuration (plan docs/plans/2026-11-13-long-horizon-task-family-and-seed-plan.md, Task 3). Every value and rule below comes from the plan's D1 to D7 or from a kit file, as each group's `source` says. Not frozen while `pending` is non-empty: `manifest.py write --freeze` refuses. The owner's allowance shares, hours and meter readings are not in this file, by the plan (D4, D7).

attempt.source: plan D2 (what an attempt is); recordings.json (the t2a-* harness arguments); fixtures token-three-tools-normal-end, -medium, -high (init event); fixtures/requests/t2a-normal-*.json (declared tools, effort)
attempt.cli_install: through the harness's own path, inside the agent container; nothing is mounted and the host's CLI is never used
attempt.version_evidence: the init event's claude_code_version; another version is a stop
attempt.not_set_rule: Simple mode is not set. The advisor and fallback switches exist in the binary, but no recording shows their effect, so none is set. The CLI's switch that makes a session wait out a usage limit is not set: a session that meets a limit ends at once (D2; RECORDINGS.md names the switches).
attempt.init_event_rule: An init event with any other tool list is a stop: a deny list lets through whatever it does not name (D2).
attempt.declared_tools_rule: the same declared tools on every request (D7, the smoke)

harness.source: plan D2 (harness and limits), D1 (host-side steps); record.sh (agent arguments, token-mode environment, base URL); recordings.json (t2a-* harness arguments); oracle_check.sh (the process limit file); RECORDINGS.md, Reproduce (the containers override)
harness.agent_setup_timeout_multiplier_source: the 33 Task 2a recordings of the CLI (the ladder's configuration) used 3; the two Task 2a oracle probes and the earlier recordings set none (D2; coordinator ruling, 2026-11-14)
harness.rule: Equal at every effort level: the task's own agent limit (28,800 s for all 16) and verifier limit, multiplier 1; its CPUs and memory; a process limit of 4,096; the dollar cap of D4 (D2).

host_side.rule: Host-side steps change no task file and are part of the method (D1).
host_side.image_name: pulled by digest under the docker.io/ full name
host_side.sub_id_range: widened, with no container running (owner question 4)

tasks.source: plan D1 (task list, identity, caps table, qualification rule); tasks.json (names and digests); report docs/reports/2026-11-13-long-horizon-benchmark-survey-and-feasibility.md section 3 (public mean USD per trial at effort max)
tasks.identity: A task is the same task when every file of its package equals the benchmark's published 4.1.0 digest, with task.toml compared after removing exactly two keys: the agent phase's network mode and its allowed hosts (D1).
tasks.digests: tasks.json, per task: digest_4_1_0, environment_image, verifier_image (each image by digest); covered by the manifest
tasks.images: the ones 4.1.0 pins, pulled by digest; nothing is built (D1)

qualification.under: the 4.1.0 package and its two pinned images, the final network policy, the ladder's CPU set at its concurrency of four, the load below the gate of D2

tasks.dropped: A task that fails the rule and has no host-side fix is dropped. It is not replaced and its 15 slots are not given to other tasks (D1).

variant.label: vba-userform-port-uidfix
variant.use: only if the owner does not run `podman system migrate` (owner question 4, the owner's decision): the unchanged task's verifier dies on this host (Errno 22, a uid above the 65,536 mapped ids), so neither half writes a reward
variant.change: tests/app_worker.py line 55, secrets.randbelow(1000000000) to secrets.randbelow(55000), in the package and in a verifier image derived from the pinned one; nothing else differs (file by file)
variant.label_rule: a modified task with its own configuration label (D1: an image other than the pinned one is a different label); never pooled with vba-userform-port
variant.record: tasks.json, vba-userform-port, variant (built once by uidfix_variant.py; oracle_check.sh checks the image id before each launch)
variant.source: coordinator ruling and plan ledger row 'Task 2b fix round 1' (7b07fa7d)

withholding.record: tasks.json, each task's withholding (the full result, the rulings' text with each ruled item); written by image_check.py tasks from image_measure.json

caps.source: plan D4 (per-attempt cap) and the D1 table
caps.formula: max(floor_usd, multiple x public_mean_usd_at_max), rounded to the cent
caps.rule: Per-attempt cap: `max(3.00, 3 × the task's public mean cost per trial at effort max)` (the table in D1), the same at every effort, enforced by the passthrough and by the CLI's own budget limit (D4).
caps.overshoot: one response: each guard acts one response late (D4)

price.source: plan D4 (price rule, settled); price_rule.json; price_check.py; orchestrator/providers/price_table.json
price.rule: orchestrator/providers/price_table.json at the frozen commit, by SHA-256, gives every rate but the five-minute write, which the criterion adds (D4).
price.per_request: one row per message id; every rate times the multiplier above the threshold of prompt tokens (input + cache read + cache write) of that request; each cache write at its own lifetime's rate

worst_case.applies_to: a 200 whose usage the meter cannot read whole, or a request that got no status back
worst_case.prompt_tokens: the larger of the request body's size in bytes and the prompt the stream's message_start reported
worst_case.long_prompt: the multiplier when that prompt is above the threshold
worst_case.then: the row is flagged worst_case and starts close (usage incomplete)
worst_case.rule: an upper bound while the vendor counts no more prompt tokens than that; the live probe's first-request prompt figure checks it (D4)

classification.source: plan D5 (the table, the paragraphs above and below it); fixtures/ (each row's cited fixtures, cut from the recordings indexed in recordings.json); stub_api.py (the stand-in's usage-limit headers, signal 1 of D4)
classification.started: A session has started when its stream holds an init event (D5).
classification.read_from: The ending is read from five things: the result event's terminal_reason, api_error, api_error_status and stop_reason; the lh-passthrough: prefix in the result text; and the passthrough's log. The log is the authority for a usage limit met before the session's ending (row 10). It is read for the slot, except for the refusals it logs with no slot (rows 12 and 13): there the reason in the attempt's own result text decides, and the tranche's rows in the attempt's time window corroborate it. A refusal is logged with no slot when it is decided before the token is mapped to a slot (passthrough_log.slot); such a row is the attempt's by passthrough_log.join. subtype decides nothing. The harness class decides nothing where endings share one; it is read only in the three rows that name it as deciding (D5): rows 1, 2 and 3.
classification.order_rule: The rows are tried in order and the first match decides, except that row 13 is tried first, so that a stop whose cause the attempt's own slot shows (classification.own_stops; the answer withheld for paid extra usage among them) is a stop whatever else the slot's log holds, a usage-limit answer among them; then row 10, because the passthrough's log is the authority for a usage limit met before the session's ending, so that row 10 decides over every ending it can meet (order_resolves); and row 14 is tried before rows 11 and 12: behind the passthrough, a vendor 401 sets the tranche stopped, so the CLI's retries meet `lh-passthrough: tranche stopped` and the attempt ends in row 12's form (D5).

order_resolves.reason: a slot whose log holds signal 1 before the ending is cut whatever the CLI's result says (coordinator rulings M1 and N1, 2026-11-14)
a vendor 401 behind the passthrough ends in row 12's form; row 14 names the cause
a usage limit met before the ending fired (the time limit) cuts the attempt; one met only by its requests after the limit does not (coordinator ruling N1, 2026-11-14)
a usage limit met before the budget stop cuts the attempt (coordinator rulings M1 and N1)
a usage limit met before the context limit cuts the attempt (coordinator rulings M1 and N1)
a usage limit met before the refusal cuts the attempt (coordinator rulings M1 and N1)
a usage limit met before the output limit cuts the attempt (coordinator rulings M1 and N1)
a usage limit met before the slot's cap cuts the attempt (coordinator rulings M1 and N1); the natural order gives the same
a usage limit met before the tranche's total or stop cuts the attempt; the natural order gives the same
a usage limit met before a vendor 401 cuts the attempt; the 401 still stops the tranche (stops); the natural order gives the same

a usage-limit 429 that carries an overage sign is withheld (D4), and the attempt is a stop, not a cut: paid usage is the one event the owner must hear of before anything resumes (coordinator ruling, 2026-11-14)

fields.harness: the harness's result of the trial; absent when the harness wrote none
fields.harness.exception: its exception type, null when it raised none (fixture key harness_exception)
fields.stream.events: the number of events in the agent's stream; 0 is no stream (fixture key n_events)
fields.stream.api_retry: the number of system events of subtype api_retry (fixture key n_api_retry)
fields.stream.system_subtypes: the subtypes of the stream's system events, in order
fields.stream.rate_limit: the rate_limit_info of each rate_limit_event, in order
fields.result: the stream's last event of type result; absent when there is none
fields.result.*: that key of the result event; absent when the result event or the key is
fields.passthrough.requests: the passthrough's log rows for the attempt's slot (classification.passthrough_log), each read by the keys of passthrough_row_keys
fields.passthrough.requests_before_ending: the slot's rows whose time is earlier than the session's ending: the moment the launcher received the stream's result event or, for a session with no result event, the moment the harness's time limit fired (the end of its agent phase); every row of the slot when neither was recorded (coordinator ruling N1, 2026-11-14)
fields.passthrough.own_stops: the causes in classification.own_stops that the slot's own rows show, as a list of their names; [] when none
fields.passthrough.tranche_requests: the passthrough's log rows of the whole tranche in the attempt's time window (classification.passthrough_log), read the same way; refusals the passthrough logs with no slot are found here, so rows 12 and 13 also require their reason in the attempt's own result text (coordinator ruling M2, 2026-11-14)

tests.a literal: the field is present and equal to it
tests.{\"absent\": true}: the field is absent (absent is never read as null)
tests.{\"null\": true}: the field is present and null
tests.{\"in\": [...]}: present and one of the values
tests.{\"not_in\": [...]}: absent, or none of the values
tests.{\"lacks\": s}: a string that does not contain s
tests.{\"some\": p}: a list with an element that p matches
tests.{\"none\": p}: a list with no element that p matches; {} matches every element, so {"none": {}} is an empty list
tests.patterns: a literal equals; "*" is present with any value; an object matches an object holding each of its keys with a matching value

own_stops.paid extra usage: a row of the slot with passed_on false: the answer withheld (paid_usage.withheld)
own_stops.token in a log row: a row of the slot with withheld: a form of the token was in the row (passthrough_log.withheld_rule)
own_stops.response model: a row of the slot whose response_model is neither the bound model nor null

classification.own_stops_source: coordinator ruling on the re-review's minor n1, 2026-11-14; passthrough.py (on_headers, settle, _append)
classification.own_stops_not_read: Three of the passthrough's stops leave no mark on the slot's rows, and their events in tranche.jsonl name no slot: a form of the token in a response, a response that cannot be checked, an unreadable slots file. An attempt that meets one ends in `tranche stopped` and is row 12; the stop itself halts the tranche (stops).

passthrough_log.source: passthrough.py on main (718617bb, the merge of feat/lh-passthrough): its docstring's State section, _row, settle, do_POST, send_error and _Server.process_request
passthrough_log.file: requests.jsonl in the passthrough's state directory (--state): one JSON row per request, appended; the meter (a restart sums it)
passthrough_log.slot: the slot's name; null in a refusal decided before the bearer token is mapped to a slot: the request line, the headers, an unknown token or a stopped tranche at the mapping, http.server's own refusals, the connection cap
passthrough_log.status: 403 in a refusal; the vendor's status in a forwarded row; null when no status came back
passthrough_log.refused: the reason (refusal.reasons, refusal.form_reasons); absent in a forwarded row
passthrough_log.limit: for a cap's refusal, the limit that acted: cap_usd or cap_requests (slot cap reached), total_usd or total_requests (tranche total reached)
passthrough_log.headers: the logged response headers by lower-case name: every anthropic-* header, retry-after, x-should-retry, request-id, content-encoding and the --paid-usage names
passthrough_log.passed_on: false when the answer was withheld for paid extra usage; the client then got `tranche stopped`
passthrough_log.withheld_rule: a row in which a form of the token appears keeps only the keys of withheld_row, withheld being the form; the tranche stops
passthrough_log.events: tranche.jsonl beside it: close_starts and stop (the passthrough's), stop and resume (the launcher's or a person's), each with its time

join.requests: the rows whose slot is the attempt's
join.tranche_requests: every row whose time lies in the attempt's window, from its slot's opening to its closing (credential.slot)
join.slotless: a row with a null slot is read only through tranche_requests: it is the attempt's when its reason is the one the attempt's own result text names (lh-passthrough: <reason>) and it lies in the window; two attempts open at once can both read one such row, and each still needs its own result text to name the reason

observation.reward: the verifier's; 0 when the verifier gives none (it ran after a timeout kill)

cut.rerun: at the head of the queue when starts reopen; the rerun is a new counted start

pre_session_failure.rerun: relaunched at most twice; lost after the third failure

stop.tranche: halts: no new start; nothing resumes until a coordinator row in the ledger names the cause and the decision
stop.rule: A stop halts the tranche: no new start. The attempt in which it occurred is not an observation and is not scored. It counts against the 240 and the USD 200, as every start does (D4: every start's settled cost is committed, and launches stop at 240 starts); for row 2's second form, which ends before a session, that is the conservative count. Its slot is not run again, and nothing resumes until a coordinator row in the ledger names the cause and the decision (D5).
stop.count_source: starts and usd: D4 (committed is the settled cost of every start; a launch only while starts < 240) and the approval (at most 240 attempts, ceiling USD 200); for row 2's second form, which ends before a session, this is the conservative count (coordinator ruling, 2026-11-14)

ruling.tranche: the launcher pauses for a recorded ruling
ruling.count_source: D4: every start's settled cost is committed

classification.classes_rule: An observation counts against the 240 and the USD 200 and enters k and n with the verifier's reward, 0 if the verifier gives none. An infrastructure failure counts against both and is excluded from k and n, listed, never scored zero; its slot is not run again. A pre-session failure counts against neither; the slot is relaunched at most twice and is lost after the third failure. An attempt cut by a usage limit is an infrastructure failure with one difference: its slot is run again, at the head of the queue, when starts reopen (D5).

rows.ending: The CLI read no credential, or the harness found none
rows.note: a stop: the configuration is wrong

The CLI's requests after the limit, until its container stops, are metered into the attempt (credential.slot; fixtures/after-limit/t2a-timeout-low.json). The fixture is a loop of tool calls the CLI refused locally, not a hung command (D5).

rows.ending: The host, Podman, the passthrough or the launcher died

rows.note: Signal 1 of D4 for the slot in the passthrough's log, in a row timed before the session's ending, decides, whatever the CLI's result says; a usage limit met only by requests after the ending (the after-limit tail of a time-limit session) does not change the attempt's row, and still closes starts (coordinator ruling N1, 2026-11-14); row 10 is tried first after row 13 (order_rule). recorded_form holds the CLI's two recorded forms: with both signals (token mode), and with signal 1 alone, an ordinary 429 after ten retries (recorded in key mode, where the CLI does not read the headers as a limit; no token-mode recording of that form exists). Signal 2 alone matches no row before 16 and pauses (coordinator ruling M1, 2026-11-14).

rows.ending: The passthrough refused: the slot's cap
rows.note: the priced cap and the optional request count (credential.slot) end alike: the row's limit (cap_usd or cap_requests) is not read

rows.ending: The passthrough refused: total or stop
rows.note: the total by either limit (total_usd or total_requests); a stop whose cause the attempt's own slot's rows do not show (classification.own_stops_not_read among them); one they show is row 13

rows.ending: The passthrough refused: model, tool, path or unknown token; and the refusals of a request outside the frozen shape; or the attempt's own slot stopped the tranche
rows.shared_why: an attempt whose own slot stopped the tranche (the answer withheld for paid extra usage, a token in its log row, another model named) reaches the CLI in the form recorded for `tranche stopped` (row 12's fixture); the slot's own rows tell it from row 12 (passthrough.own_stops)

rests_on.why: no recording sent a request outside the allowlist through the CLI; the CLI met the one 403 form for seven reasons (the cap, the total, the stop, model, tool, path, unknown token) and each time ended at once with the message in its result text; an alternative for a form reason is that recorded form with its own reason. A session that ends otherwise (a connection cut before it reads the refusal) falls to the row its ending matches, or to row 16

rows.note: each reason is required in the attempt's own result text and read from the tranche's rows in the attempt's time window, since the passthrough logs some refusals with no slot (passthrough_log.slot; coordinator ruling M2, 2026-11-14). A stop here means the request itself was outside the frozen shape or configuration; the load refusals are row 15 (coordinator ruling N2, 2026-11-14). The last three alternatives are stops whose cause the attempt's own slot's rows show (classification.own_stops; coordinator ruling on n1): the answer withheld for paid extra usage (coordinator ruling, 2026-11-14), a token in a log row, a response naming another model. Row 13 is tried before row 10; the stop's definition is unchanged, and after a withheld answer the coordinator row that lets the tranche resume also records what the owner said
decided by the vendor 401 in the passthrough's log; recorded_form is the CLI's own form without a passthrough (two retries, no refresh request), which the fixture shows

rows.ending: Provider fault, after the CLI's ten retries; or the passthrough refused under load or timing

rests_on.why: no recording shows the passthrough's load refusals through the CLI; each is the one 403 form, recorded for seven reasons (row 13's model refusal is the one cited), with its own reason

rows.note: only when the slot's log holds no usage-limit signal before the session's ending (that is row 10); the plan's `stub-rate-limit-…` names both stub-rate-limit fixtures. The last three alternatives are the passthrough's load refusals (refusal.load_reasons): it raises them under load or timing, not for a request outside the frozen shape, so they are infrastructure failures of the attempt and do not halt the tranche (coordinator ruling N2, 2026-11-14); three in one tranche pause it for a ruling (stops)

classification.recovered_faults: A normal ending can hold faults the CLI recovered from: each retry leaves an api_retry event. They change no class; their count (stream.api_retry) is recorded per attempt (D5).

cases.when: no reward after a normal ending
cases.then: a reward then stands; a verifier timeout twice is reward 0; still no reward file is an infrastructure failure

cases.when: a task on the load-sensitive list returned reward 0 while the load was above the gate during verification

regrade.rule: Verifier-only regrade (no model call, the saved artifacts unchanged), in two cases. Only a reward of 0 is regraded, because the known defect of such a verifier under load is a false failure. If the harness cannot regrade on Podman, case 1 becomes an infrastructure failure and case 2 is excluded as "indeterminate" (D5).

classification.never_rerun: Model-side endings are never excluded: they are the longest and dearest sessions and come mostly from the higher efforts. A slot whose session ended in any other way is never run again, so a retry cannot turn a model failure into a pass (D5; any other way than a cut by a usage limit).

credential.source: plan D4 (the credential route, token mode, the token's path, the passthrough, a slot's lifetime); relay-compose.yaml; record.sh (the fake token's form); fixtures/requests/t2a-*.json (the messages path)
credential.route: B: a relay container on the attempt's network; the passthrough stays one host process and holds the only credential

relay.holds: no credential, no token table and no logic; the host opens no TCP port

credential.real_token: Created by the owner with `claude setup-token`; read once, at its start, by the passthrough alone; never in this file, a container, an argument, an environment, a log, a recording or a fixture (D4).

refuses: a request that declares a provider-side tool
any path but the messages path
any request line, header, body field or tool outside the allowlist of the recorded shape (request_allowlist.json, built by make_allowlist.py)
all slots together at the ceiling
any request while the tranche is stopped
passthrough.in_flight: one request per slot; a second waits until the first is metered (at most 300 s, else `slot busy`), then is checked against the caps; a third open request of the slot is refused (`too many connections`), and so is any connection beyond 16 on one socket. Each slot of the ladder has its own socket (`own_socket` in the slots file; plan Task 5, connections): <the relay directory>/<slot>/passthrough.sock, mounted by that attempt's relay alone, so a connection counts against its own attempt before its token is read; the slot's token is `unknown token` on any other socket. The main socket serves the live probe's slots
passthrough.passes_on: every vendor response, unchanged, once checked for the token's forms (token_scan.py), except the one that stops the tranche for paid extra usage (paid_usage)

slot.opens: when the launcher starts its attempt
slot.closes: when every container of the attempt is gone; only then does the launcher retire its fake token
slot.after_the_time_limit: the CLI's requests until its container stops are the attempt's and are metered into it
slot.retired_token: a request on it is an unknown token: row 13, a stop
slot.request_count_rule: Only the live probe sets one: 6 requests per slot. The ladder sets none, and its bound per slot is the priced cap (D4).

refusal.source: plan D4 (one refusal form); stub_api.py (the pt_* faults); fixtures passthrough-*-UnknownApiError (the result texts); passthrough.py on main (718617bb): every reason it refuses with
refusal.reasons_are: the seven recorded through the CLI
refusal.form_reasons_are: the passthrough's refusals of a request outside the frozen shape (the allowlist and its size limits); none recorded through the CLI; stops (D5 row 13, rests_on)
refusal.load_reasons_are: the passthrough's refusals under load or timing: a third open request of a slot or a 17th connection, a request that waited 300 s for its slot, a body that stalled; none recorded through the CLI; infrastructure failures (D5 row 15, rests_on; coordinator ruling N2, 2026-11-14)

usage_limits.source: plan D4 (usage limits are an expected ending); fixtures token-usage-limit-NonZeroAgentExitCodeError and stub-rate-limit-ApiRateLimitError; stub_api.py (the usage_limit scenario's headers)

signal_1.form: the stand-in's, written from the header names the CLI's bundle reads; the vendor's real answer is recorded the first time one occurs

usage_limits.decided_by: signal_1: the passthrough's log is the authority (D4; D5 row 10, tried first after row 13)
usage_limits.signal_2_alone: pauses the tranche for a ruling (row 16)
usage_limits.until_recorded: any 429 from the vendor closes all starts, whatever its headers
usage_limits.in_flight: each meets the vendor's answer on its next request and ends at once: a cut (row 10)
usage_limits.after_the_ending: a usage-limit answer to a request after the session's ending (the after-limit tail of a time-limit session) closes starts as any does, and leaves the attempt in its own ending's row (D5 row 10; coordinator ruling N1, 2026-11-14)

reopen.others: follow once that session's first request is answered
reopen.no_reset_named: the tranche pauses for the coordinator

paid_usage.source: plan D4 (paid extra usage must be off); fixture token-paid-extra-usage-normal-end; stub_api.py (OVERAGE); passthrough.py (PAID_USAGE, paid_signal)
paid_usage.precondition: the owner's dated confirmation that paid extra usage is off for the account, in the ledger before the live probe, the pilot and the freeze, each time
paid_usage.value_case_source: passthrough.py paid_signal: each value is lower-cased before the comparison, and an empty header is read as no header
paid_usage.added_at_start: --paid-usage HEADER=VALUE adds a sign the live probe finds (exact value)
paid_usage.passthrough_stop_scope_source: coordinator ruling, 2026-11-14; D4 as merged from feat/lh-passthrough (718617bb) states it (passthrough_stop_rule)
paid_usage.passthrough_stop_rule: The passthrough therefore stops the tranche at any response, a 429 included, that carries `anthropic-ratelimit-unified-overage-in-use: true` or an `anthropic-ratelimit-unified-overage-status` of `allowed` or `allowed_warning`; and at any response other than a 429 that carries an `anthropic-ratelimit-unified-status` other than `allowed` or `allowed_warning` (a response without that header is not stopped by it; a 429's status is the limit's own answer, D5). The stopping response is not passed on: the client gets the 403 form with `lh-passthrough: tranche stopped`, and the passthrough still reads that response to its end and meters it. (D4)
paid_usage.acts: one request late, unless ordinary responses carry overage-status (the live probe shows whether)

ceiling.source: plan D4 (reservation, settlement, what ends the tranche); AGENTS.md (the approval: at most 240 attempts, ceiling USD 200)
ceiling.committed: the settled cost of every start + every open reservation, computed under one lock
ceiling.live_probe: its priced usage is settled into committed before the first attempt
ends: nothing in flight and the next slot's reservation does not fit

settlement.rule: Settlement replaces a reservation with the largest of four figures (D4).
figures: the session file's rows priced by the rule, one row per message id
the result event's modelUsage priced at the base rates (a floor)
settlement.timeout_kill: no result event: figure 1 settles it
settlement.cut: settles like any other: its tokens were used

allowance_guard.source: plan D4 (the allowance guard reads the owner's meter); D7.2 (the pilot's figures)
outside_this_file: the owner's share of the weekly allowance kept free, F-week
the owner's share of the five-hour allowance, F-five
the hours in which the ladder may start attempts
the pilot's dollars per meter point
the pilot's raise of the reservation
the closing margin of a window
allowance_guard.no_reading: the launcher starts nothing in a window without a reading, the smoke's and the pilot's included
allowance_guard.budget: (100 - F - the reading) x the pilot's figure for that meter, floored at zero; a start only if the ladder's priced usage since the reading plus the guard's reservation for every open slot and this one fits
allowance_guard.skip_rule: A window is skipped, and reported, when its weekly reading is at or above 100 − F-week − 5: fewer than five points would be left for the ladder (five is a judgment). When the five-hour reading is at or above 100 − F-five − 5, starts wait for that meter's reset (D4).
allowance_guard.reservation: one third of the slot's cap; raised by the pilot's largest ratio of cost to that third, for every task, if any ratio is above one
allowance_guard.figure: the pilot's priced usage over the points the meter moved plus one (its cautious end)
allowance_guard.no_five_hour_figure: two attempts at a time until the owner has read that meter around a stretch in which only the ladder used the account
allowance_guard.closing_margin: the length of the longest pilot session, rounded up to the hour

utilisation_check.if: utilisation_header names a header (it is "none" when the live probe finds none)
utilisation_check.closes_starts: whenever that figure is at or above 100 − F for its window, whoever used the allowance
utilisation_check.adds: a check; it replaces no reading
utilisation_check.rule: If ordinary responses report the account's utilisation (the probe shows whether, and under which header; none is named here because no recording shows one), the launcher also closes starts whenever that figure is at or above 100 − F for its window, whoever used the allowance. It adds a check and replaces no reading (D4).

allowance_guard.readings: at each weekly reset, and before each of the owner's windows of hours opens: the weekly and the five-hour meter, with the time and each meter's reset time (D4)
allowance_guard.after_a_five_hour_reset: until the owner gives a reading for the new five-hour window, the ladder's usage in any five hours stays within (100 − F-five) × the five-hour figure; the owner's own use of that window is unseen (D4)

network.source: plan D3 (network policy), D1 (the two overlay keys); record.sh (the agent phase's keys and the recordings' hosts)
network.list_rule: The list, the same for every task and effort: the relay of D4, by name; the Python, Node and Rust package indexes; the system package mirrors of the three base distributions. A task that needs another host gets it by name in tasks.json (D3).
network.web_tools: absent: under an allowlist the harness disallows both, and the init check would show one; the passthrough refuses a request that declares a provider-side tool
network.egress_log: kept by following the sidecar's log while it lives; it names refused connections by address and port only

host.source: plan D2 (load and CPUs, concurrency), D1 (disk), D7.7
host.cpu_rule: Attempts and their verifiers run on a fixed set of 24 CPUs, by an affinity the launcher sets and its containers inherit (D2).

load_wait.then: the tranche pauses and the coordinator reports to the owner

concurrency.fewer: whenever the allowance guard leaves room for fewer; the ladder's own containers count toward the load gate

host.no_other_heavy_work: the coordinator runs no other heavy work of this session during the tranche

disk_plan.keep: all 32 pinned images for the tranche: 23.86 GB in the store (253 layers, each counted once), on /home; the same images serve every round
disk_plan.pull_order: by digest, one at a time, before the smoke: vba-userform-port first, then the schedule's order
disk_plan.between_rounds: nothing else: the harness deletes each attempt's containers, and a first-pass job directory is under 25 MB. If the labelled variant is used, its verifier image stays too (10.2 kB over its base, the pinned verifier image)
disk_plan.staging: Podman stages each pull in /var/tmp on / (ImageCopyTmpDir); a pull needs its compressed plus unpacked size above the stop on both / and /home
disk_plan.room: /home had 68.6 to 76 GB free during the first pass: about 50 GB after the pull, 30 GB above the stop. Four first-pass trials took at most 4 x 2.74 GB of free space, which leaves about 19 GB above the stop with four attempts in flight; an attempt's own writes are measured by the smoke. / is shared with other sessions: 31.0 GB at its lowest during the pass
disk_plan.stop: D1's: no start under 20 GB free on /home or /, checked before every start (the oracle and image checks stop at 25 GB)
disk_plan.recheck: at the freeze; owner question 6 if /home then has less than about 60 GB free (20 + 23.86 + 11 + 5 margin)

host.disk_plan_rule: From the sizes Task 2b states, in the ledger: the order of pulls (vba-userform-port first, then the schedule's order); what is kept between rounds; and the room left above the 20 GB stop with four attempts' output (D1).

smoke.becomes: slot 1 of round 1, if it passes
smoke.fallback_rule: If gsea-proteomics does not qualify, the smoke task is the first qualified task in `tasks.json` order that is not on the load-sensitive list (D7.1).
smoke.after: the manifest hash is frozen and in the ledger

checks.passthrough_saw: only the bound model, only the messages path, no provider-side tool, and attempt.declared_tools on every request

checks.egress_log: no connection outside the list except refused ones

checks.token_scan: nothing in its file set, and the runtime check nothing in the attempt's containers

checks.paid_usage: no rate_limit_event reports it (isUsingOverage not false) and no response header reports it

pilot.becomes: the block of rs-archive-clone in round 1; observations of the ladder, marked in the readout
pilot.fallback_rule: If it does not qualify, the pilot task is the next dearest qualified task that is unchanged since 4.0.0 (D7.2).
pilot.meters: the owner reads every usage meter the account shows before the three start and after the last ends

schedule.block: one task's three efforts, started one after another

order.rule: The order of the blocks in a round, and of the efforts in a block, is fixed by a hash of a frozen seed, the round, the task and the effort (D7.3).
order.one_seed: one frozen seed gives both the schedule's order and the block order (coordinator ruling, 2026-11-14)

schedule.skipped: the four slots already run (the smoke and the pilot)
schedule.rerun_after_a_cut: at the head of the queue
schedule.tail: When the ceiling or the 240 ends the tranche, the tail of that order is dropped, fixed before the first attempt; the launcher never skips ahead, so at most one block is left partial (D7.4).
schedule.round_1_read: stop and read after round 1; no threshold of the readout moves
schedule.no_top_up: Nothing is topped up, moved between cells or re-thresholded after the first attempt. A slot run again after a cut is not a top-up: it is one of the 240 starts (D7.8).

stops.stop: a response with non-zero usage that names another model
an init event with another CLI version, tool list or credential source
a passthrough refusal for model, tool, path, token or a request outside the frozen shape
a sign of paid extra usage (paid_usage)
stops.resumes: only after a coordinator row that names the cause and the decision and records what the owner said (coordinator ruling, 2026-11-14)

stops.stop: usage-limit answers in a row with no observation between them

pauses_that_end_by_themselves: a usage limit, until its reset

pauses_for_a_ruling_or_an_input.pause: a window with no meter reading
a limit answer that names no reset
an ending that matches no row of D5 (row 16)
attempts ended by a load refusal of the passthrough (refusal.load_reasons; D5 row 15)
pauses_for_a_ruling_or_an_input.source: coordinator ruling N2, 2026-11-14 (D7 already counts infrastructure failures)

label.is: the SHA-256 of manifest.json, which manifest.py prints
label.change: A change after the pilot's first attempt makes a new configuration label. It is allowed only to repair a safety or correctness fault; its ledger row is written before the next start and names the fault, the change and the new hash. A change before the pilot's first attempt (after the smoke) also means a new hash and a ledger row (D7.6).
label.pooling: observations under different labels are never pooled in a cell
label.outside: the allowance inputs and readings make no label

pooled.admits: the pooled label admits a task to the family; the per-effort labels are printed beside it
pooled.min_per_effort_source: encodes D6's "Per task, pooled (K of its n attempts): K = 0 is 'floor' (upper bound 21.8% at 15); 1/15 <= K/n <= 1/3 is 'screened in'; above is 'above the band'", applied when every effort has at least 4 scored observations (12 to 15 in all; printed 'screened at n of 15 attempts', with the exact interval of K of n); below that 'not screened', with the counts per effort, neither in nor out of the family; 15 is the planned count. Coordinator ruling 2026-11-14, revised after review: a screen at exactly 15 made an excluded attempt drop the task

band_effort.among: the levels with at least one success
band_effort.label: noisy, one cell of five

effort_test.over: complete (task, round) triples: all three slots observations
effort_test.test: exact one-sided sign-flip permutation test over tasks on the sum of d_i

fall_bound.of: the pooled fall from low to high, in points
fall_bound.generator: Python's random.Random(seed); each resample of the m tasks with a complete triple draws rng.randrange(m) once per task
fall_bound.resample_fall: 100 x (the resample's low successes - its high successes) / its complete triples
fall_bound.quantile: the ceil(one_sided x resamples)-th smallest resampled fall: with 10,000 resamples, the 9,500th
fall_bound.method_source: coordinator ruling 2026-11-14 (R5): frozen as readout.py built it on feat/lh-readout; the seed stays pending for the freeze
fall_bound.rule: "Not resolved" means only that no fall above that bound was ruled out; it is never read as "does not fall" (D6).

per_effort: cost per success: the cost of every start at that level over its successes, cut starts included
cost.dominated: only when another level beats it on the same sign-flip test at p <= 0.05 and has a lower mean cost; otherwise not resolved
cost.dominated_p_source: encodes D6's "An effort level is named dominated only when another level beats it on the same sign-flip test at p <= 0.05 and has a lower mean cost"; coordinator ruling 2026-11-14: the same level as the effort test
cost.allowance: the share of a weekly allowance the tranche used, in all and per priced dollar, from the owner's readings; a report that enters no rule

readout.labels: every rule reads the observations of the current configuration label alone; an earlier label's are printed in a table of their own and enter no rule
listed: flags and exclusions, per task and effort
attempts cut by a usage limit, counted per effort
readout.no_public_figure: no figure is set beside the public row's; the readout names the configuration (D2)

contamination_scan.canary_identifier: read from the task packages at run time; never written into this repository
contamination_scan.egress: per attempt, the refused addresses and their count; a refused connection excludes nothing

readout.stop_readout: a readout that ends in a stop prints no placement

filled_rule: A pending field, once filled, moves from `pending` to `filled` with the same `field` and `type` and a `source` (the commit or ledger row it came from). `manifest.py write --freeze` refuses while `pending` is non-empty, any null is left, or a filled field fails its type (array; object; string, non-empty; sha256, 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits; scalar, a non-empty string or an integer; number, an integer or a decimal) or names no source.
